title: Qualify an unreliable AtlasOps provider

bridge.applicationConcept: HTTP authentication, status codes, rate limits, timeouts, payload validation, and provider evaluation
bridge.analogyLimit: An HTTP status alone rarely establishes business cause; provider documentation, headers, payloads, and product context are also required.

buildBrief: Define AtlasOps service-health requirements, compare three providers from official documentation, test synthetic requests, and propose a provider-independent internal contract.
incidentBrief: The provider fixture rotates through 401, 429, timeout, and malformed JSON. Classify each failure, choose safe retry behavior, and preserve a usable product state.

scenario.symptoms: Four synthetic provider modes produce distinct authentication, quota, transport, and contract failures.

acceptanceTests: Three providers are compared with official docs, cost, rights, limits, support, and exit risk
The adapter distinguishes 401, 429, timeout, malformed payload, and empty success
The ADR defines retry, cache, fallback, and stop conditions
predictionQuestions: Which failures are safe to retry automatically?
Which response details must be validated before the UI trusts the payload?
defenseQuestions: Explain authentication, authorization, transport, quota, and schema failures.
Trace one provider response into the normalized contract.
Defend when AtlasOps should stop using the provider.
hints: Classify the layer before changing retry behavior.
Read status, headers, body shape, and elapsed time as separate evidence.
Normalize provider data at one server boundary rather than throughout the UI.
